_readme: Short text lines the game picks from at random. No AI needed. Each section has a _default list; add a list under a personality name to give that personality its own lines.
Placeholders: {name}, {house}, plus any extra ones noted for the section. Add as many lines as you like.
enc_* lines are short notes on how one client visit went for her (shown in the weekly report). job_* lines are report lines for the non-escort jobs.
encore: the line added when a restless lady goes another round. enc_frustrated / enc_drained / enc_like / enc_put_off: extra visit notes.
demo_lead / demo_watch: Sam's demonstration lesson ({name} = his partner). Templates; rewrite freely.
orgy_lead ({names}, {first}, {house}), orgy_pair ({a}, {b}), orgy_end ({first}), orgy_lover ({name}: a Devoted lady sharing him): Sam's group nights. Templates; rewrite freely.

gift_trinket / gift_jewel / gift_lavish ({name}, {gift} = a random trinket from people.json gifts): Sam buys her a gift with gold (her sheet → Gifts). tutor_note ({name}, {tutor}): her weekly report note when a tutor works with her. Templates; rewrite freely.

solo._note: Report line when a lady at max lust spends part of her night alone in her room instead. Shown in the weekly report.
_default: {name} disappeared to her room early one night and didn't come back down for a long while. She seemed a lot calmer afterward.
{name} locked her door for most of an evening. She came out flushed, relaxed, and tired.
Shy but earnest: {name} excused herself early one night, too embarrassed to say why. She avoided everyone's eyes at breakfast.
{name} spent an evening shut in her room with the curtains drawn. She insists she was reading.
Bookish and curious: {name} took a novel of the steamier sort up to her room and was not seen again that night.
{name} called it 'research' and locked her door. She came out with a very satisfied look and ink on her fingers.
Mysterious and aloof: {name} vanished one evening without explanation. When she returned, she was smiling to herself and offered none.
Proud and sharp-tongued: {name} decided she didn't need anyone's help with her problem, thank you, and took the evening to herself.
{name} snapped at two clients, then went to her room and slammed the door. An hour later she came out in a far better mood.
Laid-back and lazy: {name} figured the easiest solution was the one that didn't involve getting out of bed. She skipped most of one evening.
Calm and elegant: {name} retired early one evening for 'a long bath'. It was a very long bath.

modest._note: Shown on her sheet when she has the Modest trait.
_default: She'd rather keep her clothes on. When things get intimate, they get pulled aside instead, though the lewder she gets (and the more she trusts Sam), the more comes off.
She keeps her clothing on as long as she can, and she's quietly flustered if it slips. With Sam, though, she lets the bits come off by degrees, one at a time, when she's ready.
A towel, a sleeve, a half-drawn curtain: she always has something between herself and the lamplight. The more she trusts Sam, the thinner the barriers get.
She prefers to keep a layer or two on, thank you, and Sam has learned not to tease about it. Over time, with enough warmth and enough patience, she grows braver.
She's shy about being seen, so the lamps are dimmed and the blankets drawn up. When she finally lets one fall, it feels like a gift.
Her clothes stay mostly on, tugged aside rather than shed. The more comfortable she becomes, the more she reveals, and Sam notices every inch of progress with a quiet, private joy.
{name} is still breathing hard, and she hasn't let go of him. "Again," she says. It isn't really a question.
{name} props herself up on one elbow and gives Sam a long, considering look. Apparently they're not finished.
"Don't you dare fall asleep," {name} whispers, pulling him back down against her. The lamp is guttering and the night is long, and she isn't remotely finished with him.
{name} gives a slow, satisfied sigh, stretches like a cat, and then turns that sleepy, dangerous smile on Sam again. "That was lovely," she says. "I'd like to do it properly now."
Sam is reaching for the blanket when {name} catches his wrist and shakes her head, smiling. Her cheeks are flushed, her hair is wild, and she looks much too pleased with herself to stop.
For a long moment the only sounds are the rain and their breathing. Then {name} laughs softly, rolls over, and tugs Sam closer. "One more," she says. "I might even mean it."
{name}'s tail hasn't stopped moving. She nuzzles into Sam's neck, warm and insistent, and makes a small, needy sound that says she's nowhere near done.
{name} is up on her knees before Sam has caught his breath, ears forward, eyes bright. "More," she says, and climbs back into his lap.
{name}'s ears flick toward Sam, and her tail curls around his leg and holds on. She purrs, low and rumbling, and presses her forehead to his chest. It's clear the night isn't over until she says so.

A low, contented rumble fills the room as {name} nuzzles into the crook of Sam's neck, tail thumping slowly against the sheets. She's warm, and pleased, and completely unwilling to let him go anywhere.

{name}'s tail sweeps across the blanket in a long, lazy arc, and her eyes shine gold in the lamplight. "Mm," she says, and climbs on top of him with unshakable purpose. Sam gives up the idea of sleeping altogether.
Her ears twitch at every sound, but {name} is fixed on Sam alone, nosing at his jaw, her breath warm and fast. "Again," she says, in the plain way of someone who has no intention of discussing it.

late_visit._note: Opening line when a lady knocks on Sam's door late at night.
_default: Sam is doing the books by candlelight when {name} knocks. She hasn't seen a single client all week, and she's clearly been thinking about something. "Busy?"
{name} appears in Sam's doorway in her nightclothes, holding two cups of tea she clearly has no intention of drinking.
A note slides under Sam's door: "Still awake? Come find out." It's in {name}'s handwriting.

The house is quiet, the corridor lamps burning low, when Sam hears the faintest scratch at his door. It's {name}, barefoot, with a shawl over her shoulders and a look that says she wasn't going to knock but couldn't help it. "Can I come in?" she asks.

Sam is half asleep over a stack of invoices when {name} lets herself in, carrying a plate of leftover dumplings. "You missed supper," she says, setting it down. She doesn't leave, and she doesn't pretend that the dumplings were the only reason she came.

A soft knock, then another, a little braver. {name} stands in Sam's doorway with a candle, the flame bending in the draft, and her hair loose in a way he hasn't seen before. "I couldn't sleep," she says. "I thought you might be awake too."
Shy but earnest: There's a very quiet knock. {name} is standing in the hall, red to the ears, and has clearly rehearsed what she wants to say. She forgets all of it.
Bold and flirtatious: {name} doesn't knock. She just leans in Sam's doorway until he notices her. "You work too hard, boss."

sleepin_evening._note: Opening line when the lady sharing Sam's bed in the Owner's Suite proposes as they turn in. Edit freely.
_default: The lamps are low in the Owner's Suite. {name} sits on the edge of the bed, unpinning her hair, and watches Sam over her shoulder. "We could just sleep," she says. "Or not."
{name} slides under the blanket and doesn't turn her back on him tonight. Her hand finds his. "Stay up a little longer," she murmurs.
"Long day," {name} says, curling against Sam's side in the dark. Her fingers start tracing slow circles on his chest. "I have a better idea than sleeping."

The Owner's Suite is warm, the shutters latched against the night wind, and {name} is brushing out her hair at the bedside. She catches Sam's reflection in the dark window and doesn't look away. "I'm not tired," she says, setting down the brush. "Are you?"

{name} blows out the last lamp but one and slips beneath the blanket, her feet cold and her smile warm. Rain whispers on the roof, and she rolls toward him. "Tell me about your day," she says. "Then I'll tell you about mine, and we'll see."
Sam is mid-yawn when {name} puts a finger over his mouth. The room is lit by a single candle and the pale spill of the two moons through the curtain. "That yawn," she says, "is a lie. I can tell."

sleepin_morning._note: Opening line when the lady sharing Sam's bed wakes him in the morning with ideas of her own. Edit freely.
_default: Sam wakes to gray morning light and {name} propped on one elbow beside him, smiling like she's been awake a while. "Good morning," she says, and kisses him slowly.
Something warm presses against Sam's back, and {name}'s voice is a sleepy whisper at his ear. "Don't get up yet. I've got plans for you."
{name} has already pulled the covers over both their heads. "The house can wait," she says, "for a little while."

A bird is arguing with itself outside the window and the light is the soft pink of early dawn. {name} is already awake, tracing the line of Sam's jaw with one finger. "Don't say anything," she murmurs. "Just stay."

The bed is warm, the house is still asleep, and {name} has her cheek against Sam's shoulder, listening to him breathe. When he stirs, she lifts her head with a lazy, knowing smile. "Good," she says. "You're up."

Sam wakes to the smell of baking bread drifting up from the kitchen and {name}'s hair spread over his arm. She doesn't open her eyes. "Five more minutes," she says, in a voice that makes it clear what she plans to do with them.

client_yes._note: Second half of a report highlight when a client got the service he asked for.
_default: They disappeared upstairs for most of the evening.
He came downstairs an hour later looking dazed and very satisfied.
The door stayed closed a long time. He tipped generously.
She came back down first, humming. He followed, red-faced and grinning.
The lamp in the upstairs window burned late, and the piano downstairs had finished two full sets before the door finally opened.
He went up with a nervous cough and a rumpled hat, and came down an hour later carrying the hat and no memory of where he'd left his dignity.
Somewhere between the second glass of plum wine and the stairs, he made up his mind. The staircase creaked for a while afterward, and nobody pretended not to notice.
They slipped away from the crowded lounge while the fiddler was mid-song. By the time the tune ended, the evening had gone somewhere much quieter.
He spent a long, unhurried evening behind a closed door and emerged looking like a man who'd forgotten what day it was. His coin purse, on the other hand, remembered perfectly.
The room smelled of lavender and warm candle wax by the time they were done, and the bedsheets looked like they'd lost an argument.

client_company._note: Second half of a report highlight when a client only wanted her company.
_default: He left lighter in the purse and very happy about it.
He promised to come back next week.
He told three friends about her before he got home.
He lingered on the stairs, patting his pockets like a man who didn't want to leave, then bought a bottle of wine for the road.
He stopped to straighten his collar in the hallway mirror and caught himself smiling at his own reflection.
He paid, he tipped, and he tried to tip again at the door. Sam had to gently steer him outside.
He left humming a tune from the lounge and walked straight into a lamppost. He apologized to it.
He lingered over his last cup of tea in the lounge, reluctant to let the night end, and asked the doorman which evenings were quietest.
He wrote her a small, terrible poem on a napkin before he left. She kept it.

lover_waiting._note: Opening line when a lover (Devoted) at max lust comes to Sam instead of handling it herself.
_default: {name} is sitting on the edge of Sam's bed when he gets back, shoes off, very much not reading the book in her lap. "You've been busy all week," she says. "I've been patient."
Sam finds a note on his desk in {name}'s handwriting: "My room. Tonight. Don't make me come get you."
{name} has made herself comfortable in Sam's chair, feet up on his desk, reading his ledger upside down with great ceremony. "Your handwriting is awful," she announces. "Come here. I've missed you."

The lamp in {name}'s window is lit when Sam passes her door, and the door is open a hand's width, which is as close to a summons as she'll ever write down. He stops. She says, from inside, "Don't pretend you didn't see."

There's a tray on Sam's bed when he returns: tea, two cups, and a single flower in a water glass. {name} is sitting beside it, trying very hard to look casual. "I thought we might have some time," she says. "If you're not busy."
{name} intercepts Sam on the stairs, takes his sleeve, and doesn't say a word until they're at her door. "Everyone is very busy," she says then. "I decided you could be busy in here."
Shy but earnest: {name} hovers in Sam's doorway, fidgeting with her sleeve. "I, um. I waited. For you. All week." She's bright red.
Proud and sharp-tongued: {name} corners Sam in the hall. "I don't beg," she says. "So you're going to notice on your own that it's been a week."

lover_reunion._note: First line of the scene when Sam goes to a lover who's been waiting.
_default: She pulls him in by the collar and doesn't let go for a long time.
"Finally," she breathes, and the door clicks shut behind them.
She's been counting the hours, and it shows in the way she crosses the room: quickly, then slowly, as if she's remembered she's supposed to be composed. It lasts about a second.
"You're late," she says, with absolutely no heat. Then she kisses him, and neither of them mentions it again.
The lamp is low, the room is warm, and she's waiting for him with her arms already open. He walks into them like a man coming home.
She hooks a finger through his belt and leads him in without a word. The door shuts, the latch drops, and the corridor is left to its rumors.

good_night._note: Report line after a week where her clients loved her.
_default: {name} had a great week and knows it. She's in a very good mood.
Cheerful and teasing: {name} spent breakfast bragging about her week to anyone who'd listen, with impressions of her clients.
Shy but earnest: {name} didn't say much, but she kept smiling to herself all week. Someone said she did well and she turned bright red.
Proud and sharp-tongued: {name} reminded everyone, twice, that she is the best in the house. Nobody argued.
Hot-blooded and competitive: {name} has started keeping a tally of satisfied clients on the kitchen wall. She's winning.
Bookish and curious: {name} has notes on what worked this week. Detailed notes. She'd like to discuss them.
Warm and motherly: {name}'s clients left happy, and she made a point of making sure the other girls did too.
Mysterious and aloof: {name} said nothing about her week. Her clients said plenty.
Laid-back and lazy: {name} had a good week with surprisingly little effort, which she considers the ideal week.

bad_night._note: Report line after a rough week with unhappy or difficult clients.
_default: {name} had a rough week. A couple of clients left unhappy, and so did she.
Shy but earnest: {name} had a bad client this week and has been very quiet since. She keeps apologizing for nothing.
Proud and sharp-tongued: Two of {name}'s clients complained. {name} complained louder, and is now refusing to speak to anyone.
Hot-blooded and competitive: {name} took a bad week personally. She's been training twice as hard out of spite.
Cheerful and teasing: {name} laughed off a bad client, but the jokes have been a little thinner this week.
Laid-back and lazy: {name} had a bad week and shrugged it off. Mostly.
Mysterious and aloof: Something about this week bothered {name}. She won't say what.

lover_jealous._note: When one of Sam's lovers has been left out for weeks while another hasn't. {other} = the other lover.
_default: {name} has noticed exactly how many evenings Sam has spent with {other} lately, and exactly how many he's spent with her. She'd like to talk.
Shy but earnest: {name} hasn't said anything. She's just been very quiet whenever {other} is around, and Sam finally notices.
Proud and sharp-tongued: "I'm not jealous," {name} announces, apropos of nothing, while glaring at {other} across the room.
Hot-blooded and competitive: {name} has started treating {other} like a rival. Breakfast has become very tense.

lover_shared._note: When two happy lovers come to Sam's room together. {other} = the second lover.
_default: There's a knock at Sam's door. It's {name}. Then a second knock: {other}, right behind her. They look at each other, then at Sam, and seem to reach an understanding without him.
{name} and {other} arrive at Sam's door together, arm in arm, as though they'd rehearsed it. They probably did. "We have an arrangement," {name} says, and {other} nods solemnly, hiding a grin.
Sam opens his door to find {name} and {other} in the corridor, whispering. They stop the moment they see him and share a look that says everything. "We'd like to come in," {other} says. "Both of us."

{other} comes in first, shy and a little flushed, and {name} follows close behind to shut the door. They exchange a glance of perfect understanding, which leaves Sam out of it entirely. He decides not to mind.
"No arguments," {name} says, steering {other} by the elbow into Sam's room. "We've settled it between ourselves." {other} just smiles, wickedly, and sits on the bed.

Two sets of footsteps in the corridor, one knock, and then {name} and {other} are standing in his doorway, giggling like conspirators. Whatever they have planned, they've clearly been planning it for days.

breakup._note: When Sam ends things with a lover. She stays on at the house.
_default: {name} listens without interrupting. "Okay," she says finally. "I'll be fine. Just... give me some time."
Shy but earnest: {name} nods too fast and says she understands, then excuses herself. Nobody sees her for the rest of the day.
Proud and sharp-tongued: "Fine," {name} says crisply. "Your loss." She makes it all the way to the hallway before her voice cracks.
Warm and motherly: {name} squeezes his hand. "You're allowed to change your mind, love. I'm not going anywhere." She cries later, alone.
Hot-blooded and competitive: {name} throws a cup at the wall. Then she apologizes to the cup. Then she leaves.
Laid-back and lazy: {name} shrugs a little too casually. "Sure. Whatever works." She doesn't come down for dinner.
Mysterious and aloof: {name} says nothing at all. She just looks at him for a long moment, then nods once and goes.

rekindle_yes._note: When an ex-lover agrees to try again.
_default: {name} pretends to think about it for exactly three seconds. "Took you long enough."
{name} looks at him for a long while, then lets out a breath she seems to have held for weeks. "Yes," she says. "Obviously yes. Don't make that face, you're going to cry."
"I was hoping you'd ask," {name} admits, smiling in a way that goes straight to her eyes. "I'd have asked you myself, but I wanted to see you work for it."
{name} takes his hand in both of hers. "I've missed this," she says quietly. "I've missed you. Yes. Let's try again."
{name} pretends to consider, tapping her chin and looking out the window. It lasts about a breath and a half before she gives up and kisses him. "Yes, you idiot."
"Fine," {name} says, trying very hard to look put-upon and failing completely. "But you're buying dinner. Several dinners."

rekindle_no._note: When an ex-lover isn't ready to try again.
_default: {name} smiles, a little sadly. "Not yet. Ask me again sometime."
{name} shakes her head gently, her eyes soft. "I care about you," she says, "but I'm not there yet. Give me some time, and be patient with me."
"Not today," {name} says, with a small, sincere smile. "It isn't you. I just need to be sure, and I'm not, not quite. Ask me again."
{name} looks down at her hands for a moment, then up. "I'm sorry," she says. "Part of me wants to say yes. The rest of me needs more time."
She touches his arm briefly, kindly, and lets go. "Ask me again when the leaves turn," {name} says. "I'll have a better answer, I promise."
{name} sighs, not unkindly. "I'm flattered. Really. But I'd be saying yes for the wrong reasons, and you deserve better than that."
She enjoyed that one.
Her favorite. She was humming afterward.
She came back downstairs smiling.
This was the one she'd have picked from the whole week, and she hummed the entire way back to her room.
She stretched out on the cushions afterward looking wonderfully pleased with herself.
She told Sam later it was the best part of her week. Sam turned very red and said he was glad.
She took her time on the stairs afterward, in no hurry to get back to work.
She was still smiling when the next lantern was lit.
Easily her favorite of the week. She kept replaying it over her tea.

enc_dislike._note: Client asked for something she dislikes but does.
_default: Not her favorite.
She got through it, but it's not her thing.
She was a little quiet afterward.
She gave him a perfectly professional evening and kept her real opinion to herself.
She counted the minutes against the candle and was glad when it was over.
She went back to her room afterward and brewed herself something strong.
She kept her smile painted on, but it took some effort.
She wasn't rude about it, but she was quick to change the subject afterward.
She was very careful not to look at the clock, and very glad to wash up after.

enc_stretch._note: A service that's still a stretch for her with clients.
_default: A stretch for her. She did it anyway.
She wasn't sure about it, and it showed a little.
Outside her comfort zone, but she managed.
It wasn't what she'd usually choose, but she gave it an honest try with a brave smile.
She took a deep breath at the door and went in determined to be professional.
Not her usual territory by a long shot, but she muddled through with good humor.
She learned something new about her limits, and decided she could live with it.
A little awkward, a little bold, and she had to laugh at herself halfway through.
She'd rather have been elsewhere, but she held her head up and finished the job.

enc_eager._note: She was in the mood (high lust).
_default: She'd been wanting it all week.
She was more into it than he was.
She was very much in the mood.
She was practically waiting at the door for him.
She'd been eyeing the clock all afternoon and was ready the moment the bell rang.
She'd braided flowers into her hair for the occasion and was not at all shy about it.
She didn't need coaxing; if anything, she was the one doing the leading.
She'd been in a good mood since breakfast and it showed.
Her enthusiasm caught him a little off guard, and then caught him entirely.
He left glowing.
He's already asking when she's free next.
He tipped well and said so twice.
He floated down the stairs with a grin he couldn't wipe off, and walked out into the night humming.
He left a tip big enough that Sam checked it twice for mistakes.
He paid for a bottle for the whole lounge on his way out.
He squeezed her hand at the door and promised to be back before the week was out.
He told the doorman that this was the best night of his life, then corrected it to 'month' and then 'year'.
He looked ten years younger and walked a little taller on the way home.
He left grumbling.
It didn't really click.
Neither of them enjoyed it much.
The conversation ran out before the evening did, and the silence was long.
The candle burned down, but the spark never really took hold.
They parted politely, each privately sure it hadn't been their night.
He checked his pocket watch a few times too many.
Nothing went wrong exactly. Nothing went especially right either.
They both shrugged it off in the hallway and went their separate ways.
She didn't mind saying no.
No hard feelings either way.
She turned him down with a friendly smile and offered him a drink at the bar instead.
She said no politely, and he took it with a gracious nod.
She waved him toward another lady, no offense taken on either side.
She told him honestly it wasn't for her, and he appreciated the honesty.
He asked, she declined, and they went on chatting as if nothing had happened.
She shook her head kindly and the conversation moved on without a hitch.

enc_nomood._note: She turned it down because she wasn't in the mood (low lust).
_default: She just wasn't in the mood.
Not tonight, she said.
She'd had a long day and her heart simply wasn't in it.
She curled up in the corner of the lounge instead, and told him so kindly.
She begged off with a small yawn and a gentler smile.
Maybe another night, she said. Tonight she wanted tea and quiet.
The spark just wasn't there, and she knew better than to fake it.
She wasn't feeling it, so she poured him a drink on the house and let him down easy.

job_bartender._note: Weekly report line for a bartender.
_default: {name} kept the drinks flowing at {house} and settled two arguments with a single raised eyebrow.
{name} invented a new cocktail this week. Half the regulars love it, the other half are scared of it.
{name} worked the bar all week and knows every regular's order by heart now.
{name} polished glasses until they sparkled and served a gruff old sailor who confessed everything. The bar at {house} heard it all.
{name} worked behind the bar of {house} all week, pouring, laughing, and quietly cutting off a very determined merchant.
{name} learned the exact hour that the crowd wants something stronger, and had it ready each time.
A busy week at the bar: {name} juggled three orders at once and still remembered to ask after a regular's cough.
{name} added a pinch of cinnamon to the house wine and had {house} talking about it for days.
{name} turned a dull Tuesday around by sliding free peanuts across the bar and telling a truly terrible joke.

job_dancer._note: Weekly report line for a dancer.
_default: {name}'s new routine had the lounge on its feet.
{name} danced every night this week. Someone threw flowers, which she pretended not to love.
A crowd gathered early for {name}'s set. The bar did well out of it.
{name} danced in the lamplight until her bells jingled, and the room kept time with its feet.
The fiddler struggled to keep up with {name} this week. Nobody minded.
{name} spun through the lounge in silk and shadows, and a few clients forgot to drink.
{name} added a slow, swaying number to her set and the whole room went quiet before it erupted in applause.
Her ankles ached by Friday, but {name} gave the crowd a finale that brought the house down.
{name} dragged a shy client onto the floor for one dance. He talked about it for the rest of the evening.

job_bath._note: Weekly report line for a bath attendant.
_default: {name} kept the baths hot and the guests relaxed.
{name} has the guests so relaxed they forget to leave. She considers it a professional achievement.
Steam, scented oil, and {name}'s soft humming. The bathhouse was busy all week.
{name} kept the water hot and the lanterns low, and the guests drifted out pink and sleepy.
{name} swept steam off the tiles all week and learned to tell a tired merchant from a lonely one by the way he sank into the water.
Fresh towels, cedar oil, and {name}'s quiet humming: the bathhouse had a very good week.
{name} tended the baths and hung herbs from the rafters, which made the whole room smell like a mountain meadow.
The soaking tubs were full every night. {name} says it's the best job she's ever had for her hands.
{name} had the pool so cozy that two guests fell asleep in the water and had to be woken gently.

job_bath_joined._note: Bath attendant comfortable enough to join bathers in the water (bath massage).
_default: {name} didn't just tend the baths this week; she got in. Bath massages, in the water, became the most requested thing on the menu.
{name} spent most of the week in the hot water with the guests, working out knots. Nobody wanted to leave the pool.
Steam, scented oil, and {name} slipping into the water to give massages where they soak. Business was very good.
{name} slipped into the warm water with her sleeves rolled and spent the week kneading shoulders. The steam swallowed every sigh.
{name} traded her towels for a seat in the bath, working knots out of tired backs while lanterns swayed above. The queue was long.
{name} spent the evenings waist-deep in the pool, hands busy and the room fragrant with oil. Guests left looking boneless.
Bath massages from {name}, in the water, with cedar smoke and soft chatter. She says her hands are sore and her heart is full.
{name} dunked herself into the baths each night, and the guests have been tipping like it's a festival.
{name} waded in among the soaking guests this week, and the most-requested spot in the whole house became the one next to her.

job_bath_more._note: Bath attendant who joined bathers and, in the mood, offered them more.
_default: {name} joined the bathers in the water, and once or twice the massage turned into something more, at her suggestion.
Bath massages in the water all week, and {name} was in such a mood that a few lucky guests got more than their backs worked on.
The baths were busy and so was {name}. When the mood took her, the massages didn't stay massages.
{name} slid into the water for massages as usual, but a few times her hands wandered where she meant them to.
The steam was thick, the oil was warm, and {name} was feeling bold. Not every massage stayed innocent.
{name} worked out the knots in tired shoulders, and sometimes the kneading turned into something slower and warmer.
Between the lanterns and the humid hush, {name} let a few of her massages drift further than the menu allows.
{name} treated a few of her favorites to a little extra under the water, and no one was in the mood to complain.
The baths were busy, and so was {name}. A few lucky guests got a massage that ended in a quiet, shared smile.

job_teacher._note: Weekly report line for the classroom teacher.
_default: {name} ran the classroom at {house} with a ruler and endless patience. Notes were taken.
{name} drilled the house until the lesson stuck. Somebody asked for homework. {name} was delighted.
{name} wrote on the slate, pointed, and waited. By evening the whole house was practising.
{name} chalked the day's lesson across the slate at {house} and ran the class with a patient, level voice.
{name} gave the ladies of {house} a hard morning of drills and an easy afternoon of practice.
{name} corrected posture, vowels, and bad habits with a gentle tap of her pointer. By Friday the house was gliding.

{names} have been whispering in the corner of {house} for an hour, and when {first} finally comes over to Sam's table, the others are right behind her. "We've come to a conclusion," she says. Sam, who has learned to dread conclusions, puts his cup down.

It begins with a card game that nobody is playing seriously, and ends with {first} announcing that the stakes have changed. {names} lean in as one. By the time Sam understands what he's agreed to, the lamps in {house} have been turned down.

The night is warm, the wine is good, and {first} has a gleam in her eye that Sam recognizes from the last three times he lost an argument. "Don't panic," she says, as {names} gather round. "It's a group project."
{a} and {b} end up tangled together more than once and don't seem to mind in the least.
{a} catches {b}'s eye across the bed and they both start laughing, then very much stop laughing.
At one point {a} is coaching {b} with a running commentary. {b} tells her to shut up, then follows every word.
{a} pulls {b} in for a kiss while they wait their turn. It turns out waiting is not the hardship anyone expected.
{a} and {b} have drifted into a corner of their own, trading whispered jokes and soft touches as if they had all night. They do.
Between rounds, {a} straightens {b}'s hair, which immediately ruins it again, and they both grin like thieves.
Much later, the bed is a wreck, the lantern has burned down, and Sam is pinned under at least three warm, sleeping bodies. He decides this is fine. This is very fine.
By dawn they're a heap of limbs and sheets. Somebody is snoring. Somebody else is still giggling. Sam stares at the ceiling, wondering how his life got here, and finds he has no complaints.
They drift off one by one. The last one awake is {first}, who props her chin on Sam's chest and says, "Same time next week?" She falls asleep before he can answer.

The candles are stubs, the wine is gone, and the sheets look like they lost a war. Sam lies in the middle of it, grinning at nothing, as {first} pulls the blanket over all of them. "Goodnight," she says, sleepy and satisfied.

Dawn finds them tangled, warm, and wholly unrepentant. Birdsong drifts in through the shutters, and {first} is the first to stir, cracking an eye to survey the damage. "Worth it," she mumbles, and goes back to sleep.

The house is silent at last. Sam takes one long look around the room, at the sleeping faces, the scattered cushions, the smile {first} wears even in her sleep, and thinks that, notes or no notes, he will remember this one.
{name} keeps a hand on Sam the whole night, sharing him and making very sure everyone knows who he goes home with.
{name} stays within arm's reach of Sam all night, a hand on his shoulder, a foot against his ankle. She shares, but she makes sure everybody knows whose he is when the lamps go out.
Whatever else happens, {name} always ends up back at Sam's side, tucked into the crook of his arm like she belongs there. She does, and she lets the room know it with one sidelong glance.
{name} is generous, laughing, and wonderfully relaxed about the whole affair, but every few minutes her fingers find Sam's and squeeze. It's a quiet, private message in a very public night.
At some point {name} whispers "mine" in Sam's ear, so softly that only he can hear. Then she turns back to the others with a bright smile and carries on as though nothing at all had been said.
{name} insists on tucking the blanket around Sam when the night is over, a small, possessive kindness. "You're coming with me," she says, and nobody argues.

private_open._note: Opening of plain private time with Sam (before the turn and the service line). {name} = her name. Act-neutral.
_default: {name} drags Sam off for a "lesson." He takes notes afterward. She finds this hilarious.
A quiet evening, a locked door, and a "do not disturb" sign that the neighbors would later call unnecessary given the noise.
{name} insists Sam needs more practice. Sam, a diligent student, does not argue.
By the time they come downstairs, everyone has very carefully decided not to look at them.

The house has settled into its after-hours hush by the time {name} finds Sam in the lounge. Rain ticks against the shutters, one lantern is still burning, and she takes the cushion right beside his instead of across from him. "Walk me upstairs?" she says, as if it were a question.

{name}'s room smells of warm tea and the cedar oil she rubs into the bed frame. She lights a single candle, pulls the curtain against the rain, and pats the quilt beside her. Sam sits with the care of a man entering a temple.

They start with the leftover plum cakes from the kitchen and a game of cards neither of them is paying attention to. Somewhere around the third hand, {name} puts her cards face down and just looks at him. The candle gutters, and nobody remembers who was winning.

The evening wind pushes the shutters open a hand's width, bringing in night-jasmine and the faraway music of the Silver Fiddle. {name} gets up to close them, changes her mind, and leaves them open. "Better," she says, turning back with a small, private smile.

Sam knocks, which is silly, because {name} invited him and is sitting right there. She raises an eyebrow at the knock, and he apologizes, and she laughs until she has to wipe her eyes. It breaks the nervous part cleanly in half, and he is allowed in.

{name} has put a kettle on the little brazier and arranged every cushion in the room into one large, suspicious nest. "Nothing is happening yet," she says, pouring. "This is just the part where we get comfortable." Her foot finds his under the blanket anyway.

The corridors are quiet, the stairs creak in their usual places, and {name} holds Sam's sleeve all the way up so he doesn't trip over the loose board. At her door she stops, turns, and straightens his collar for no reason at all. "There," she says. "Now you're presentable. Briefly."

A thunderstorm rolls over Hollowmere just as the last guest leaves, and the whole house goes dim and golden. {name} finds Sam at his desk, takes the quill out of his hand, and sets it carefully out of reach. "The ledger will survive one night," she says.

Sam has brought a lantern, a bottle of plum wine, and a plan. The plan dissolves the instant {name} opens the door in her loose robe, her hair half down. She takes the bottle, ignores the plan, and tugs him inside.

The bathhouse steam has drifted all the way up the stairs, and {name}'s skin is still faintly warm and smelling of orange peel when she greets him. She leans in the doorway, in no hurry at all. "I thought you might want some company," she says, "since you've been staring at that door for an hour."

private_first._note: Her first private time with Sam (replaces private_open once). {name}.
_default:
{name} has clearly been thinking about this. She pulls Sam into her room before he can finish saying hello.

The door closes.

{name} has clearly been thinking about this. She's tidied her room twice, changed her mind about the lamp three times, and when Sam arrives she says "Hello" in a very careful voice. Then she laughs at herself and lets him in.

There's a ribbon in {name}'s hair that wasn't there at supper. She doesn't mention it, and Sam, who has learned some things, doesn't either. The room is warm, the lamp is low, and she shuts the door behind him with a soft click and her back flat against it.

"I rehearsed what to say," {name} admits, standing in her doorway with the night breeze in her sleeves. "It was very good. I've forgotten all of it." She takes his hand instead, and her fingers are a little cold and entirely steady.

Rain is drumming on the roof tiles when {name} opens her door, and she's wearing the expression of a woman who has argued with herself for a week and won. She lets Sam come in, then stands very close, listening to the rain, saying nothing.

{name} has laid out two cups, one candle, and no excuses. She sits on the edge of her bed, folds her hands, then unfolds them. "You're the first person I've actually wanted to ask," she says quietly. "So I'm asking."

private_first_sam._note: Sam's very first time (replaces private_open once). {name}.
_default:
{name} takes Sam's hand and leads him upstairs. It becomes clear about four seconds in that his previous-life experience in this department is exactly zero.

{name} looks absolutely delighted about this.

The door closes.

Sam has read about this in two lives and practiced it in neither. He arrives at {name}'s door with his hands clasped like a schoolboy at a recital, and she takes one look at him and smiles so warmly that the nerves lose half their grip. "Come in," she says. "I'll go slowly. I'm very good at slowly."

"I should mention," Sam begins, in the lamplit hush of {name}'s room, "that I have no idea what I'm doing." {name} puts a finger to his lips, delighted beyond words. "Good," she whispers. "Then nothing gets in the way of me showing you."

{name} takes charge the way she might take a shy guest's coat, gently and without making a fuss of it. She guides his hands, tells him to breathe, and tells him he doesn't have to be graceful. The moons are bright in the window, and Sam's ears are the color of boiled shrimp.

Sam stands at the threshold with the posture of a man about to take an exam. {name} laughs, soft and kind, takes his notebook out of his coat pocket, and sets it on the shelf. "No notes this time," she says, drawing him inside. "Tonight, you just learn it by heart." The door closes behind them.

train_service._note: Hands-on service practice with Sam (followed by her shown service's private_act line). {name}.
_default: {name} decides Sam's education is a shared project. They work through everything they're comfortable with, one thing at a time, until both of them are confident in the technique. Sam takes notes afterward. She finds this hilarious.

Sam brings a candle, a notebook, and the serious face he wears for exams. {name} brings a smirk and a very good memory of what she's comfortable with. They run through her repertoire one item at a time, stopping whenever she says "wait, try it like this," and he writes it all down.

It's supposed to be a practice session, and for the first ten minutes it very nearly is. {name} corrects his hand placement, he asks a polite follow-up question, and she tells him that politeness is lovely but he can stop checking in every four seconds. The notes are getting messier.

The practice room smells of lamp oil and warm cedar, and {name} has put cushions everywhere. "Think of it as a rehearsal," she says. Sam thinks of it as an exam he's thrilled to be taking. They work through each service she's sure of, polishing and adjusting.

Sam has drawn a small diagram. {name} looks at it for a long, silent moment, then tells him it's anatomically ambitious and takes the pencil to correct it. After that they do things the hands-on way, and the diagram gets very smudged.

"Rule one," {name} announces, "no giggling at the technique." They break that rule within a minute. Between laughs, they go through each service she's confident in, trading adjustments, and the lamp burns down while they wrestle with the finer points.

The rain beats a steady rhythm on the shutters while {name} walks Sam through her own repertoire like a guide leading a tour. She stops at each service, shows him what works and what doesn't, and gives him her expert verdict on his form. He scribbles frantically, glowing with pride.

train_skill._note: One-on-one trade-skill training, keyed by skill (service, dance, bar, combat, manage; _default fallback). {name}, {skill}. Followed by "Sam takes detailed notes, as is tradition."
_default: Sam walks {name} through the trade the hands-on way, {skill} first: posture, pacing, the little things regulars notice.

Sam pulls up a stool, and {name} sits across from him with the focused expression she saves for things she wants to be good at. They work through {skill} slowly, one piece at a time, and he is careful to praise what she does well before he mentions anything else.

The afternoon light slants across the floor while Sam and {name} drill {skill} together. She tries it, misses, tries again; he offers a small suggestion; and she gets it on the next go with a bright, startled laugh.

"Show me," Sam says, and {name} does, and then he shows her his own clumsy version for contrast. She's helpless with laughter, which is the best thing that could have happened. After that, {skill} goes much more smoothly.

They keep at {skill} until the lamps need trimming. {name} is stubborn and quick, and Sam is patient, and somewhere in the middle of it she stops looking at him as the boss and starts looking at him as a very good teacher.
service: Sam and {name} sit across from each other with a pot of tea and a plan: how to greet a guest, how to read a mood, how to make a tired stranger feel like the only person in the room. She practices her welcome on him four different ways. By the fourth, he is genuinely flustered.

"Eye contact first," Sam says, "then the smile, then the offer of a drink." {name} nods, tries it, and gets it right on the third go. The lounge is empty and quiet, the afternoon light coming slantwise through the shutters, and she sits a little taller each time he nods.

They spend the afternoon on small things, which turn out to be the big things: how to pour wine without a drip, when to stay silent, when to ask a question. {name} is quick, and the quiet pride on her face grows every time Sam says "yes, exactly that."

Sam plays the nervous first-time guest. He is, unfortunately, very convincing. {name} manages to settle him with a few well-chosen words and a warm hand on his sleeve, and then they both realize he's forgotten to keep the act up.
dance: The parlor rug is rolled aside and {name} stands barefoot on the boards while Sam counts the beat aloud. He can't dance, but he can spot where her weight drifts, and he's learned to say so gently. She keeps rolling her eyes and correcting herself anyway.

A phonograph does not exist in this world, so Sam hums and taps the rhythm on a table, badly. {name} laughs, then takes the beat from him and makes it hers, turning slowly across the floor. By the end of the hour, the humming is the only thing out of tune.

"Again from the top," Sam says, and {name} salutes with a flourish and starts the routine over. Her shadow sweeps long across the wall in the lantern light, and her footwork sharpens every time. She stops at the end, breathing hard, flushed and pleased.

Sam watches from a stool at the edge of the floor, chin in his hand, offering notes like a very polite critic. {name} adjusts a spin, lifts her arms a touch higher, and the whole thing suddenly flows. He claps once, startled into it, and she bows with a grin.
bar: Behind the empty bar, the shelves of bottles glint in the lamplight. Sam sets out three glasses and a jigger, and {name} learns to measure by eye while he times her pours with a sand-glass. She spills the first one, grins, and wipes the bar with a flourish.

"A good bartender remembers faces," Sam says, holding up a deck of sketched regulars. {name} studies them, names each one correctly, and adds what each of them drinks. He is unreasonably impressed. She is unreasonably smug.

They go through the shaker, the strainer, and the long spoon, one tool at a time. {name} gets the ice rattle just right on her fifth try, and the sound rings through the quiet room like a small bell. Sam makes her do it six more times, to be sure.

Sam mixes a drink badly on purpose so {name} can fix it. She tastes it, winces, and rebuilds it from the base up, adding a twist of citrus and a pinch of something he doesn't recognize. It tastes wonderful, and he asks her to show him again.
combat: The yard behind the house is damp from morning rain, and {name} stands in the middle of it with a wooden practice blade in her hand. Sam, who is thin and nerdy and very serious about this, demonstrates a stance. She straightens his, kindly, and then shows him how it's done.

They spar slowly, the wooden blades clacking in the morning stillness. Sam calls out corrections he read once in a book, and {name} humors him for exactly as long as it takes to disarm him. "Theory is lovely," she says, handing his stick back. "Now try it with feet."

{name} runs the drill again and again, footwork first, then guard, then the long step in. Sam counts for her, and the count keeps time with her breathing. By the end her shirt is damp and her grin is sharp.

Sam doesn't know a great deal about fighting, but he knows how to pay attention. He watches {name} move, notices where she drops her guard, and says so, apologetically. She tests the notion, finds it true, and gives him a surprised look of real respect.
manage: Ledgers, receipts, and a pot of strong tea cover the office desk. Sam walks {name} through the weekly accounts one column at a time, and she follows with a finger down the page, frowning, then brightening when the numbers click. "So this is where all the candles go," she says.

"A manager's job," Sam says, "is to make problems small before they're big." {name} considers this seriously, then asks three sharp questions about the rota that he has to look up. She pretends not to enjoy that.

They role-play a difficult guest. Sam plays the guest, loudly and a bit unfairly, and {name} de-escalates him with a calm voice and a firm smile. He folds in under a minute. She sits back, pleased, and takes the last biscuit.

The window is open to the afternoon, with the noise of the street drifting in, and {name} is working out next week's schedule on a slate. Sam leans over to point out a clash, and she has already spotted it. "Give me some credit," she says, rubbing it out.
